title: Merge Close Characters
summary: Given a string s consisting of lowercase English letters and an integer k , identify any two equal characters in the string that are within k positions of each other.
statement: Given a string s consisting of lowercase English letters and an integer k , identify any two equal characters in the string that are within k positions of each other. Merge the right character into the left character one at a time, updating the string after each merge. Continue this process until no more merges are possible. Return the resulting string. If multiple merges are possible at the same left index, perform the merge with the smallest right index first.
constraints: s is a nonempty lowercase string and k is nonnegative.
Repeatedly delete the right member of the first equal-character pair whose current indices differ by at most k.
Continue on the shortened string until no qualifying pair remains.
hints: Only characters that survive affect all later updated positions.
Build the final string left to right and remember each character’s most recent surviving index.
Skip a character when its current output index is within k of that survivor; otherwise append and update its index.
Earlier survivors implement the required leftmost merge order, and skipped characters never occupy positions in the evolving string.
editorial: Earlier survivors implement the required leftmost merge order, and skipped characters never occupy positions in the evolving string.

tests.explanation: The two a characters are three positions apart, so the right a merges away and abc remains.
Distinct indices are never within distance zero, so aa remains unchanged.
